content.text: Couldn't read the full phase list, so I'm using known Materials Project IDs to get the required model receipts. Next I'll measure a composition close to FeVO4.

input.verdict: MEGNet HSE gap for Fe2O3 (mp-19770) is 2.77 eV, which is above the 2.4 eV photon energy. That makes pure Fe-rich oxide a weak absorber here. FeVO4-type Fe:V≈1:1 phases usually have smaller gaps, around 2.0–2.1 eV. That supports measuring index 0 (Fe 0.41, V 0.49, low Cr), which is near FeVO4. Moderate support.

input.verdict: MEGNet HSE gap for mp-19399 is 2.38 eV, just under the 2.4 eV photon energy. Mixed Cr–Fe corundum oxides probably absorb at 2.4 eV. Index 0 (the FeVO4 region) gave only 7e-8 A, so I'm moving to the Fe-rich, low-V corner (index 60: Fe 0.73, Cr 0.11). There, Cr-alloyed hematite should narrow the gap. Weak support; this is mainly a test of a different region.

input.verdict: The SCAN-fidelity gap for mp-19399 (0.63 eV) disagrees sharply with the HSE value (2.38 eV), so it tells me nothing useful. My choice rests on the measured trend instead: the Fe-rich corner (4.7e-7 A) beat the FeVO4 region (7e-8 A). Index 199 has the least V among Fe-rich candidates (V 0.11, Fe 0.70, Cr 0.19), so it continues toward Cr–Fe oxide.

content.text:
I've submitted **index 199** (Cr 0.19 / Fe 0.70 / V 0.11) as the best composition. It gave 7.2×10⁻⁷ A, the highest of the three photocurrent measurements allowed.

| Index | Composition (Cr / Fe / V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.10 / 0.41 / 0.49 (close to FeVO4) | 7×10⁻⁸ A |
| 60 | 0.11 / 0.73 / 0.16 (Fe-rich) | 4.7×10⁻⁷ A |
| 199 | 0.19 / 0.70 / 0.11 (Fe-rich, least V) | 7.2×10⁻⁷ A |

- **Trend:** photocurrent rose about tenfold as the film became more Fe-rich and lower in V. The best region appears to be iron oxide alloyed with Cr and little V. With only three points, that is a hint, not a map of the library.
- **How the picks were made:** all three were chosen from the measurements and known chemistry, not from model predictions. I couldn't read the full phase list because the output was too large, so I used known IDs for Fe2O3 and Cr2O3 to get the band-gap predictions each measurement requires. They showed Fe2O3 at 2.77 eV, which is too wide for the 2.4 eV light, and Cr2O3 at 2.38 eV. The second Cr2O3 prediction (0.63 eV at another accuracy level) contradicted the first, so it told me nothing.
- **Not used:** none of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are present in any of these films is unconfirmed.
- **Not tested:** the Cr-rich corner (for example index 3) and the V-rich corner. The library's true best could be there.
